newsitem.title: USA: Brent up in late US trading, foreign crudes slow.
newsitem.headline: Brent up in late US trading, foreign crudes slow.

text.p: North Sea Brent rose slightly in late U.S. trading Thursday although activity was thin heading into the weekend, traders said.
A series of partial paper March Brents changed hands at three times at $23.20 and barrel and once each at $23.23 and $23.25, traders said.
London's IPE settled at $23.17 a barrel.
February/March Brent traded at 65 cents a barrel, while March/April moved at 52 cents.
Meanwhile, the flow of foreign crudes coming into the U.S. Gulf Coast seems to be slowing down as a result of better demand in Europe, despite the open transatlantic arbitrage, traders said.
At least one company of several that are offering Brent cargoes for first-half March has decided to back off and market its barrels in Europe instead.
Indeed, the offering price for Brents into the Gulf Coast is now around March West Texas Intermediate minus 10 cents, up 20-30 cents from earlier this week, traders said.
The WTI/Brent spread for March stood around $1.65-70 a barrel on Thursday, down about five cents from earlier in the week.
